title: Bachmann's conjecture on relations among Schlesinger–Zudilin $q$-multiple zeta values
statement:
Let $\mathcal{U}$ be the alphabet used to form the noncommutative word algebra $\mathbb{Q}\langle\mathcal{U}\rangle$, let $\mathbb{Q}\langle\mathcal{U}\rangle^\circ$ be the subspace spanned by words not starting with $u_0$, and let

$$
\zeta_q^\mathrm{SZ}\colon \mathbb{Q}\langle\mathcal{U}\rangle^\circ\to\mathbb{Q}\llbracket q\rrbracket
$$

be the Schlesinger–Zudilin $q$-multiple-zeta-value map, with image $\mathcal{Z}_q$. The algebra carries the **stuffle product** $\ast$, and it has the involution **duality** $\tau$ defined on words by

$$
\tau\left(u_{k_1}u_0^{z_1}\cdots u_{k_d}u_0^{z_d}\right)=u_{z_d+1}u_0^{k_d-1}\cdots u_{z_1+1}u_0^{k_1-1}.
$$

**Bachmann's conjecture.** All $\mathbb{Q}$-linear relations among elements of $\mathcal{Z}_q$ are generated by the stuffle product $\ast$ and duality $\tau$. This conjecturally gives a complete description of the linear relations among Schlesinger–Zudilin $q$-multiple zeta values, while the general completeness of these two families of relations remains open.
source_name: Benjamin Brindle, “Combinatorial interpretation of the Schlesinger-Zudilin stuffle product”, arXiv:2409.16966 (2025).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.16966

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2024).
